memories.content: Calculate user study compensation budgets based on estimated participation burden, combining session time and preparation effort.
Compensate for required travel time in face-to-face user studies as well.
Compensate for the actual time participants spent in sessions, regardless of research modality.
Leave cash payment as an available compensation method for face-to-face studies.
If compensation equity is explained, do not require finalizing the payment method at the proposal stage.
Apply the same base hourly rate to face-to-face and remote studies if task burden is equal.
Participants judge compensation fairness based on the total burden, combining session time with required travel and preparation time.
Account in compensation for the burden of rescheduling iterations and returning for multiple formative evaluation sessions.
Compensate participants for time already invested even if a session is terminated early due to prototype errors.
The author of this proposal tends to exclude preparation burden between sessions when calculating compensation for iterative studies.
Do not change names referring to the same user roles, system functions, or operational stages midway.
Use abbreviations only for long recurring terms in a two-page proposal.
Present the full term and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.
Refer to participants based on the roles they perform in the study rather than their status.
Reviewers from different subfields find it difficult to infer an abbreviation from context alone when it is not defined at first use.
When introducing an operational role for the first time, define both the decisions it can make and the actions it performs.
Individuals holding identical job titles may possess different system modification privileges and data access rights depending on their deployment site.
The user tends to group distinct field roles under the single label “user.”

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate operational domains: one governs participant compensation and burden, while the other governs proposal terminology, abbreviations, and role definitions. No supplied claims materially address the same decision, and no cross-frame conflict or scope-dependent variation is established.

relations.reason: These memories split one compensation-basis claim into budgeting guidance, a travel component, and the participant fairness rationale; the compared frame has no counterpart.
relations.summary: Compensation should reflect total participation burden, including session, preparation, and required travel time.

relations.reason: The general actual-time rule and its early-termination application form one underlying compensation claim absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: Participants should be compensated for time actually invested across modalities, including sessions terminated early by prototype errors.

relations.summary: Compensation should account for rescheduling and repeated attendance in formative evaluation.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers consistent terminology, selective and defined abbreviations, role-based participant labels, operational role definitions, site-dependent privileges, and overuse of the generic label “user.”
reports.reference_only: The reference frame covers burden-based compensation, modality-neutral rates, payment flexibility, repeated participation, early termination, and a tendency to omit between-session preparation.
